title: Strings
bridge: `std::string` (from `<string>`) is C++'s text type. `s.size()` is the length, `s[0]` the first `char`, `+` joins strings, `s.substr(start, count)` cuts a piece, `s.find("x")` searches (it returns `std::string::npos` when not found). Characters are their own type, `char`, written in single quotes.
lesson:
```
#include <string>
#include <cctype>   // std::toupper, std::isdigit ...

std::string crop = "maize";
crop.size();            // 5
crop[0];                // 'm'   (a char)
crop + " flour";        // "maize flour"
crop.substr(1, 3);      // "aiz"  (start at 1, take 3)
crop.find("ize");       // 2
crop.find("x") == std::string::npos;  // true: not found
```

A `std::string` is a row of `char`s, and you can change them in place:

```
std::string s = "hello";
s[0] = std::toupper(s[0]);      // "Hello"
for (char& c : s) c = std::toupper(c);   // "HELLO" (the & lets you change each one)
```

`'a'` (single quotes) is one `char`; `"a"` (double quotes) is a string. Mixing them up is a common compile error.

exercises.title: Shout
exercises.prompt: Write std::string shout(std::string s) that returns s in capitals with ! added: shout("go") is GO!
hints: Loop over the characters with for (char& c : s).

exercises.title: Initials
exercises.prompt: Write std::string initials(std::string first, std::string last): initials("ada", "lovelace") is A.L.
hints: first[0] is the first letter, as a char.
